method: Power over Ethernet sends direct current down the twisted pairs, and the cable resistance turns part of the supply voltage into heat before the powered device sees it. A conductor of the given gauge has resistance R' = rho / A per metre, with annealed copper rho = 1.724e-8 ohm-metres at 20 C and the cross-section taken from the AWG diameter d = 0.127 mm * 92^((36 - n)/39); that gives about 0.0842 ohm/m for 24 AWG and 0.0668 ohm/m for 23 AWG. Current leaves the switch on one pair and returns on another, and each pair is two conductors in parallel, so a 2-pair standard has loop resistance R_loop = R' * L. When all four pairs carry the load (802.3bt Type 3 and Type 4) the two paths sit in parallel and R_loop = R' * L / 2. A powered device behaves as a constant-power load, because its input drives a DC-DC converter, so the current rises as the voltage sags: solving V_pd = V_s - I * R_loop together with P = V_pd * I gives I = (V_s - sqrt(V_s^2 - 4 * R_loop * P)) / (2 * R_loop), the smaller of the two roots, and V_pd = P / I. A negative discriminant means no operating point exists and the run is refused as unable to deliver the load. The voltage drop is V_s - V_pd and its share of the supply is quoted in per cent; the cable loss is I^2 * R_loop; delivery efficiency is the device power divided by the power sent. Each class guarantees a minimum device voltage: 37.0 V for 802.3af (12.95 W, 350 mA over two pairs), 42.5 V for 802.3at (25.5 W, 600 mA over two pairs) and for 802.3bt Type 3 (51 W over four pairs, 600 mA), and 41.1 V for 802.3bt Type 4 (71.3 W, 960 mA over four pairs). The margin is the device voltage minus that floor, and the longest run is where the device sits exactly on it: (V_s - V_floor) / ((P / V_floor) * R' / 2) for a four-pair run. Supply voltage runs from 44 to 57 V, load power from 0.1 to 100 W, each conductor gauge from the four listed AWG sizes, and the run from 1 to 200 metres or 3.2808 to 656.168 feet, with one foot exactly 0.3048 metres. Inputs accept at most four decimals and no sign or exponent notation; blank, malformed and out-of-range values are refused with a field-specific message. Notes rather than errors cover a device below the class floor, less than 1 V of headroom, a run past the 100 m TIA-568 channel limit, a supply below the class minimum, a load above the class guarantee and a current above the class limit. The model assumes steady state, 20 C copper, a uniform cable and no connector, patch-lead or bundling losses, so treat the result as a planning estimate. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: IEEE 802.3af, 802.3at and 802.3bt Power over Ethernet: source output voltage ranges and the minimum voltage guaranteed at the powered device (37.0 V, 42.5 V and 41.1 V), with the class power and pair-current limits for Type 1 to Type 4.
TIA-568 structured cabling: the 100 m channel limit and the 22 to 26 AWG solid-copper conductors used by Cat5e, Cat6 and Cat6A cable.
NIST and IEC 60228 conductor data: annealed copper resistivity 1.724e-8 ohm-metres at 20 C and the AWG diameter relation d = 0.127 mm * 92^((36 - n)/39).
